standard_prerequisites.name: Classification of classes by extensions and the projective bundle of the extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology, the lemma identifying first cohomology classes with extensions of the structure sheaf, and Divisors, the lemma describing the conormal sheaf of the section of a projective bundle defined by a surjection
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the extension corresponding to a nontrivial class, its projective bundle and the section whose conormal sheaf is the structure sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: Affineness of the complement of the section and finiteness of an affine proper morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard properties of projective bundles: the complement of the image of a section is affine; Morphisms, the lemma that an affine and proper morphism is finite, and the lemma that a finite birational morphism onto a normal scheme is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the contradiction argument showing that the two sections must meet, and the normality step for the scheme theoretic image.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of normalization for Nagata schemes and Cartier divisors from sections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, the lemnas that normalization of a Nagata scheme is finite and that the image of a section of a smooth morphism is an effective Cartier divisor, and Divisors, the consequence that the pullback to the normalization is again a Cartier divisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the normalized scheme, the Cartier divisor obtained by pulling back the section, and the computation of the conormal sheaf on the normalization.

standard_prerequisites.name: Impossibility of a nontrivial invertible conormal sheaf on such a divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma asserting the nontriviality obstruction for the conormal sheaf of the Cartier divisor obtained above
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final contradiction, which proves the injectivity.

core_obligations: Translate a nontrivial class into geometry (proof lines 1701-1724): represent a nontrivial class in the first cohomology by an extension of the structure sheaf by itself, form the associated projective bundle and the section induced by the surjection onto the structure sheaf; if the class restricts trivially to the inverse image of the open, the splitting there defines a second section over that open, disjoint from the first.

Show the second section must meet the first (proof lines 1724-1740): the scheme theoretic image of that second section would otherwise be an affine and proper morphism onto the normal scheme, hence finite, hence birational finite onto a normal scheme and therefore an isomorphism, contradicting the nontriviality of the class.

Pass to the normalization and compute the conormal sheaf (proof lines 1740-1754): since the base ring is Nagata the normalization of the scheme theoretic image is finite; the pullback of the Cartier divisor given by the first section is a nonempty Cartier divisor contained in the closed fibre, and the conormal sheaf of the section being the structure sheaf of the base, the conormal sheaf of its pullback on the normalization is invertible with the same trivialization; this contradicts the obstruction lemma for such divisors and hence the restriction of the class is injective.
proof_roadmap: Replace a nontrivial cohomology class by an extension and its projective bundle, and use triviality of the restriction to build a second section.
Show the second section must meet the first, otherwise its scheme theoretic image would be a finite birational morphism onto a normal scheme.
Normalize, pull back the Cartier divisor and compute the conormal sheaf to obtain the contradiction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that in the vanishing situation, for a normal source over a Nagata base, the restriction map on the first cohomology of the structure sheaf to the inverse image of the open is injective (statement lines 1691-1699). The proof (proof lines 1701-1754) turns a nontrivial class into an extension and its projective bundle, uses triviality of the restriction to produce a second section, shows that it must meet the first by an affineness and finiteness argument, and finally normalizes and computes a conormal sheaf to reach a contradiction. H3: a geometric argument with several reductions, written out in full.
